hard.funny_explanation: When a book knows you're too tired to read, so it gives you pretty pictures to look at while you pretend to be smart.

examples.text: The illustrated edition of the novel made the fantasy world much easier to imagine.
I prefer the illustrated menu because I need to see exactly how tall my burger is going to be.

hard.real_world_analogy: A comic book version of a heavy science textbook.

words.meaning: Single people considered separately from their group.

medium.simple_explanation: Single people, rather than groups or organizations.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'onesies' of the human race—just one person doing their thing.

examples.text: Several individuals contributed their private photo collections to the book.
I prefer to work with individuals, mainly because groups make it harder to hide the snacks.

words.meaning: Companies or people who prepare and issue books.
People who write books, articles, or stories.
Relating to the original inhabitants of a place.

medium.simple_explanation: Belonging to a particular place by birth or origin.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'original flavor' people or plants of a specific spot on the map.

examples.text: The book 'The Native Americans' tells the history of the original inhabitants of North America.
I am a native of my bedroom; I know every square inch of the floor under my bed.

words.meaning: The study of past events and people.
Relating to different groups based on shared physical traits.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to different groups of people based on their shared physical characteristics or heritage.
medium.funny_explanation: A word for the ways humans have tried to sort each other into different 'teams' throughout history.

examples.text: The book explores the racial laws used in Germany during the 1930s.
History class teaches us that racial divisions were often used to create unfair rules.

words.meaning: The start of something's existence or life.
Forming a mental image of something in the mind.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used in the title 'Visualizing Indian Women', referring to how women were represented or seen in history through images.
hard.simple_explanation: The act of forming a mental picture of something or making something visible through art or data.
hard.funny_explanation: Basically, it's daydreaming with a fancy name, like when you imagine yourself winning an Oscar while brushing your teeth.

examples.text: Visualizing the data helped the scientists understand the growth of the forest.
I'm currently visualizing a world where homework does itself.

hard.real_world_analogy: Closing your eyes and trying to 'see' the route to your favorite pizza shop.

words.meaning: Material that provides official information or evidence.

medium.simple_explanation: Official papers or records that provide evidence or proof of something.
medium.funny_explanation: The giant pile of paperwork you need to prove that what you said is actually true.

examples.text: The archives provided documentation for the events described in the chapter.
I have no documentation to prove I brushed my teeth, but I promise I did!

words.meaning: The physical appearance of the natural features of an area.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Mentioned in the title 'Topography of Terror', referring to the physical or structural layout of a historical site.
hard.simple_explanation: The detailed mapping or description of the physical features of an area, like hills, valleys, and buildings.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like looking at a map that cares about how bumpy the ground is, rather than just where the roads are.

examples.text: The topography of the region made it very difficult for the army to move their heavy equipment.
The topography of my bed changes completely when the cat decides to sleep right in the middle.

hard.real_world_analogy: A 3D model of a mountain range that shows every single peak and dip.

words.meaning: Information used to promote a specific point of view.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Referenced in the title 'Politics and Propaganda' regarding the Nazi regime's use of information to control people.
hard.simple_explanation: Information, often biased or misleading, used to promote a particular political cause or point of view.
hard.funny_explanation: When your younger sibling tells your parents you're 'dangerous' just because you didn't share your chips—that's sibling propaganda.

examples.text: War-time propaganda was used to convince citizens that the enemy was pure evil.
The cafeteria's poster claiming the 'mystery meat' is a superfood is clearly propaganda.

hard.real_world_analogy: A TV commercial that tells you a sugary cereal will give you superpowers.

words.meaning: To a great or significant degree.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text states that some sections 'draw substantially' from specific research papers, meaning they rely heavily on that work.
hard.simple_explanation: To a great or significant extent; basically, a whole lot.
hard.funny_explanation: If you say you 'substantially' finished your meal, it means there isn't even a crumb left for the dog.

examples.text: The new evidence substantially changed the outcome of the trial.
My mood improves substantially the moment I hear the ice cream truck.

hard.real_world_analogy: Replacing a tiny cup of water with a giant bucket.

words.meaning: Parts that something is divided into.
Relating to society or its organization.
Legal right to control the use of creative work.

medium.simple_explanation: The legal right that gives the creator of a work the power to control how it is used.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'No Stealing My Ideas' law that keeps people from printing your drawings on t-shirts without asking.

examples.text: The publisher contacted all copyright holders before using the photographs.
I'm putting a copyright on my new dance move so nobody can use it at the party.

words.meaning: People or organizations having the power to make decisions.

medium.simple_explanation: People or organizations that have the power to make decisions or enforce rules.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'Big Bosses' who make the rules and make sure everyone is following them.

examples.text: The authors reached out to the concerned authorities to get permission for the text.
The playground authorities (also known as teachers) say we can't play tag today.

words.meaning: Someone or something that has been left out.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The authors state that any 'omission' of copyright credit will be fixed later.
hard.simple_explanation: The act of leaving something out or forgetting to include it.
hard.funny_explanation: Like when you list all your friends in a 'thank you' speech but forget the one person who actually gave you the pen to write it.

examples.text: The omission of his name from the guest list caused a huge argument.
The omission of sugar in this cake makes it taste like a literal sponge.

hard.real_world_analogy: A puzzle that is missing exactly one piece right in the middle.

words.meaning: Put right or corrected a mistake.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The publisher promises that mistakes will be 'rectified' (corrected) in future printings.
hard.simple_explanation: Put right; corrected or fixed.
hard.funny_explanation: The fancy way of saying 'I messed up and I'm fixing it now so please don't be mad.'

examples.text: The bank rectified the error in my account by returning the missing money.
I rectified the situation of the broken vase by hiding the pieces under the rug.

hard.real_world_analogy: Using a 'Delete' button on a typo or an eraser on a math problem.

words.meaning: Formal attention or information about something happening.
Short written records used to remember or record information.
To produce more copies of a previously printed book.

medium.simple_explanation: To produce more copies of a book or document that has already been published, usually with few or no changes.
medium.funny_explanation: When a book is so popular (or everyone lost their copy) that the printing press has to do a 'round two' to keep up with the demand.

examples.text: The school ordered a reprint of the science textbook for the new semester.
The cat's autobiography was such a hit that the publisher had to order a third reprint immediately.
